overview: This joint resolution would end the national emergency the President declared on February 1, 2025, in Executive Order 14193, which cited illegal drugs and migration across the northern border and was used to put tariffs, or import taxes, on goods from Canada. The National Emergencies Act lets Congress end a declared emergency by passing a resolution like this one. Ending the emergency would remove the legal basis for the measures taken under it. The House passed it on February 11, 2026; it would still need to pass the Senate and be signed by the President, or have a veto overridden, to take effect. As of February 12, 2026, it had been sent to the Senate Finance Committee.
for: Supporters say Congress, not the President, should control tariffs, and that using emergency powers to tax imports from a close ally raises prices for American families and businesses.
against: Critics say the emergency gives the President leverage to press Canada on drug trafficking and border security, and ending it would weaken that pressure.
